$comment: Machine-readable requirement inventory; the generated compliance-report.md is its human-readable view. tools/compliance-gate.ts fails the build if any id here has zero passing tests, or if a test references an id-shaped tag absent from this list.

namespaces.9449: RFC 9449 (DPoP) normative statements that apply to a resource server
namespaces.AL: Antlion-native requirements: the README's common-mistakes list and the package's own guarantees

requirements.summary: The DPoP header value is token68 carrying one compact JWS.
The proof header's typ is dpop+jwt.
The proof alg is never none and never a MAC algorithm.
The proof's jwk never contains a private key.
The proof payload carries jti, htm, htu and iat.
A proof presented with an access token carries ath.
Check 1: there is not more than one DPoP header.
Check 2: the DPoP header is a single well-formed JWT.
Check 3: every claim section 4.2 requires is present.
Check 4: typ is dpop+jwt.
Check 5: alg is a registered asymmetric algorithm, not none, and acceptable to local policy.
Check 6: the signature verifies with the public key in the jwk header.
Check 7: the jwk header does not contain a private key.
Check 8: htm matches the request method.
Check 9: htu matches the request URI, ignoring query and fragment.
Check 10: when the server provides nonces, the nonce claim is one it provided.
Check 11: the proof's creation time is inside an acceptable window.
Check 12: ath is the hash of the presented token, and the token is bound to the proof's key.
htu is compared after RFC 3986 syntax-based and scheme-based normalization.
cnf.jkt is compared to the RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the proof key.
A DPoP-scheme token is accepted only with a DPoP proof checked per section 4.3 and bound per section 6.
Access is never granted unless every check succeeds; there is no partial result.
A refusal is 401 with WWW-Authenticate: DPoP and an error parameter when a token was presented.
The challenge carries an algs parameter listing the accepted proof algorithms.
A DPoP-bound token presented under the Bearer scheme is refused.
A challenge to a request with no credentials carries no error code.
Server nonces are 1*NQCHAR.
A response carrying DPoP-Nonce is marked Cache-Control: no-store.
A response never carries more than one DPoP-Nonce.
Nonce values are unpredictable without the server's secret.
A resource server asks for a nonce with 401, WWW-Authenticate: DPoP error="use_dpop_nonce" and DPoP-Nonce.
A nonce is accepted only by the server that issued it.
Proofs are accepted only for a limited time after creation.
jti values are stored as a fixed-size hash, so a large jti cannot exhaust the store.
With nonces on, a proof without a nonce is refused.
Only asymmetric algorithms deemed secure sign proofs; none is never allowed.
A DPoPVerifiedJwt exists only after the binding check; no proof-only verifier is exported.
The thumbprint is computed by jose from the verified proof key, never read from input; RFC 7638 and RFC 9449 vectors pass.
A DPoP profile refuses the Bearer scheme outright.
A token without a well-formed cnf.jkt is refused under the DPoP scheme.
Embedded-key verification lives in one module and cannot verify an access token.
A proof jwk with d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, oth or k is refused.
The algorithm allowlist is fixed to the FAPI set, and alg must match the jwk's key type, curve and size.
RS256 proofs are accepted only through antlion-lacewing/legacy.
The proof typ is enforced.
Two DPoP or two Authorization headers, joined by Headers with a comma, are refused.
The DPoP scheme is matched in any case and followed by one or more spaces and one token68 (RFC 9449 figure 12).
A proof header or payload that names a member twice, at any depth, is refused, read by Lacewing's own parser.
Header parameters that name another key or change JWS processing are refused.
htu is compared exactly against the configured origin plus the request path; Host and forwarding headers are never read.
htm is compared exactly, case included.
ath is always required and is the SHA-256 of the exact token string presented.
The iat window has a hard ceiling, and the future allowance is small and fixed.
maxProofAge defaults to 60 seconds and cannot exceed 300; the future allowance is 5 seconds; both edges are inclusive.
The replay store is required by the profile's type; the in-memory store is named for one process.
The store contract is one atomic addIfAbsent; a store error or non-boolean result refuses; the TTL covers the whole iat window.
The store is consulted last, after both signatures and the binding pass.
The replay key is the proof key's thumbprint plus the jti, so proofs from different keys never collide.
Nonce mode has no default; nonces are stateless HMACs that expire, rotate, and verify on every node sharing the secret.
Antlion builds the use_dpop_nonce challenge itself.
Checks run in a fixed order: size, structure, typ/alg/htm/htu, proof signature, token, binding, freshness, store.
The client sees only the RFC error value; the precise reason is a typed code, and messages never repeat request content.
An error from the caller's own code that Lacewing does not catch passes through unchanged; only Antlion's and Lacewing's refusals become AntlionErrors.
Every profile and store option is validated at construction, with a message naming the fix.
The Node adapter sees duplicate headers through headersDistinct and the path the client signed under Express routers, Fastify prefixes and koa-mount.
The header names a browser client needs in CORS are exported and documented.
The docs say DPoP does not protect a compromised client, hide the token, or work without state.
